svg.title: The four pieces in play during one red-green-refactor cycle
svg.desc: Four panels arranged in a rectangle — the failing test, the implementation under construction, the refactor step, and the regression suite — each labelled with the guarantee it provides, with arrows running clockwise between them and a band underneath stating the invariant the loop preserves.
svg.text: One cycle: the four pieces, and what each one guarantees
Read the arrows clockwise. Nothing here is optional; drop a piece and the guarantee under it goes with it.
1 · The failing test
Written before the code it calls. Names the
function, its arguments and its answer while
none of the three exists yet.
Guarantees: the contract was authored
deliberately, not read back off the code.
2 · The implementation under construction
Grows only in answer to a test that is red
right now, and only by the least code that
turns that one test green.
Guarantees: no branch exists that no test
ever asked for.
3 · The refactor step
Structure changes; behaviour does not. The
same tests pass before and after, in the same
number, or it was not a refactor.
Guarantees: the design can improve without
a fresh round of checking by hand.
4 · The regression suite — the safety net
Every test that has ever gone green, re-run
on every single cycle. It is the accumulated
output of every earlier lap of this loop.
Guarantees: this change did not quietly
undo a behaviour decided last week.
then tidy
the run that proves it
next behaviour
The invariant that makes the loop worth the trouble
Every test in the suite has been watched failing for a stated reason, and then watched passing.
A test that has only ever been green is evidence of nothing — it may be wired to nothing at all.
